subject: Marketplace addendum — pass-through evidence & invoice flow clarification
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@cloudvault.io>

Cc: legal@cloudvault.io
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace addendum / pass-through obligations — initial redlines

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the discussion last week. Attached are CloudVault's initial redlines to the Marketplace Addendum (PDF) and a short vendor evidence request (DOCX) that our procurement team needs before we can complete the financial pass-through flow. High level items: 

- We need clearer language describing who issues invoices to end-customers vs. who bills CloudVault (pass-through vs reseller).
- Pass-through liability carveouts (taxes, chargebacks) — your redline currently leaves open whether Redwood or marketplace bears certain tax-withholding risks.
- Audit/evidence: our accounting wants a short list of artifacts (invoices, settlement reports, signed order forms) and desired retention window.
- Indemnity and limitations: if the marketplace collects fees on our behalf, we want a simple mechanism for a billing reconciliation and a contract-level liability cap tied to net fees.

Can you confirm Redwood's support model here (do you provide invoice-level settlement reports and a signed orderbook export) and whether you can accept a 3-year retention for settlement evidence?

I'm copying our legal mailbox so they can track the thread. We'd like to get to a mutual form by next Friday (21 May) if possible.

Attachments: CloudVault_MSA_redline_v3.pdf, vendor-evidence-request.docx

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Head of Partnerships
CloudVault, Inc.

Samantha — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Ben (sales/ops) to coordinate.

Quick answers up front:
- Redwood supports issuing settlement reports at invoice line level; we can produce a signed orderbook export for reconciliation.
- Retention: 3 years is standard and acceptable for settlement evidence; we can export CSVs and provide secure Drive links on request.
- Taxes/chargebacks: we prefer pass-through of marketplace-levied taxes to the end customer, but we recognize CloudVault may ask for a carveout — Karthik, see below for proposed language.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Karthik to propose narrow pass-through clause (by EOD Wed).
2) Ben to map billing flow and confirm which party issues the invoice and where the tax fields appear in our settlement reports (by Thu).
3) Samantha/legal to confirm evidence checklist and any internal acceptance criteria (by Fri).
4) Final mutual form and DocuSign link target: 21 May.

I've attached a quick mapping worksheet we use for evidence handoffs — fill in any missing items and we'll update.

Attachments: MPA_evidence_mapping.xlsx

Best,
Ava Chen

Ava/Samantha — putting a narrowly scoped pass-through sentence on the table to reduce back-and-forth. This is intended to be operationally precise rather than legal-heavy.

Suggested clause (for the addendum):
"For amounts collected by the Marketplace on behalf of the Parties, Redwood will provide invoice-level settlement reports and remittance to CloudVault. Taxes and statutory withholdings charged by the Marketplace shall be passed through to the end-customer; Redwood shall not be liable for taxes properly imposed by a third-party Marketplace, provided Redwood timely provides reasonable supporting evidence to CloudVault upon request. Disputes as to remittance shall be subject to the reconciliation procedure in Section X and shall be limited to adjustments to amounts actually collected and remitted during the applicable settlement period."

Notes/asks: 
- Is CloudVault comfortable with a reconciliation-first approach (adjust amounts vs. full indemnity)?
- For audit scope, we propose: invoice PDFs, line-item settlement CSVs, signed order form export, and proof of remittance (bank/ACH trace) for the disputed period. Retention: 36 months.

I attached a text file with the clause to make redlining easier. If you want a more aggressive vendor-side indemnity we can discuss, but that will need procurement signoff.

Attachments: pass-through_clause_suggestion.txt

-Karthik
Legal Counsel
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — the suggested clause looks good as a starting point. A few notes from procurement/legal: 

- Reconciliation-first approach: acceptable, provided CloudVault is given a 45-day window from receipt of settlement reports to raise disputes.
- Evidence checklist: invoice PDFs, settlement CSV, signed order form, proof of remittance (bank trace) — retention 36 months: agreed.
- Invoicing flow: CloudVault will be the billed customer in the marketplace UI for reseller-sold seats; Redwood will provide the settlement export and remittance.

I'll have our counsel incorporate Karthik's clause with two small edits (45-day dispute window; explicit mention of 'chargeback fees') and send a redline by close of business Monday. If we can get that, procurement will route the DocuSign and we can aim for signature the week of 24 May.
